heading: SVX2 FastROM Animated Video
lede: Ten seconds and all 300 frames of a real NASA Artemis launch camera reel, compressed as SVX2, decoded by hand-tuned 65816 assembly, and animated at a verified 30 fps through Mode 7 in a genuine 1 MiB Fast HiROM cartridge image.
keysHtml: Self-running — the ROM validates the complete stream and every bank-crossing packet, then continuously plays all 300 Artemis frames.
doc:
What this proves

The cartridge immediately animates a Mode 7 title while it walks the complete 300-frame stream, stages packets from banked HiROM into high WRAM, and target-validates every packet that crosses a 64 KiB ROM-bank boundary. After the title spins out, one SVX2 keyframe and 299 in-place deltas play through an NMI-counted scheduler.

Cartridge-native dashboard

The SNES changes PPU modes at scanline 192: Mode 7 presents the video above, while a conventional Mode 1 BG3 tilemap renders TIME, measured FPS, and health state below. The dashboard is generated by the cartridge—not browser chrome and not pixels burned into the footage.

30 fps full-pipeline result

The post-title emulator regression charges packet DMA, assembly decode, dashboard updates, and presentation DMA. It records 716 presentations in 2,400 VBlanks, covers more than two complete ten-second loops, and reports zero decoder errors and zero deadline slips.

Source footage: NASA Artemis I press-site camera, November 16, 2022. Hit Verify fidelity to require the cartridge's 300-frame two-loop health gate live in this tab.
